chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for the one who performs Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is like the one who visits Allah, Mighty and Majestic, above His Throne.' I said, 'So what is for the one who performs Ziyarah of one of you (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as if he performed Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَحَداً مِنْكُمْ: One of you (referring to the Imams)
key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (specifically for spiritual merit, Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Tawassul' through the Imams, establishing a spiritual hierarchy where visiting the Prophet Muhammad is equivalent to visiting Allah, and visiting the Imams is equivalent to visiting the Prophet. Scholars interpret this not as literal physical proximity to the Divine Essence, but as a metaphor for the Imams' unique status as the perfect manifestations of God's attributes and His chosen intermediaries. This chain of merit underscores the theological significance of Ziyarah as a means of drawing closer to the Divine through the Ahl al-Bayt.
